London AdvancedAbout this tool
Make the journey part of the visit

Find worthwhile detours, not another generic list.

Smart Navigation starts with your actual journey. Instead of asking you to cross London for a recommendation, it looks for interesting places close to a walking route between your starting point and destination.

You decide how far you will leave the route and which types of places interest you. The map then shows possible detours from the London Advanced collection.

Useful for
  • Making a necessary walk interesting
  • Filling time between appointments
  • Finding overlooked places nearby
  • Checking cycle docks near a route
How to use it

Build a route around your time.

  1. 01

    Enter your journey

    Choose your starting point and destination to create a walking route between them.

  2. 02

    Set your tolerance

    Choose 200 metres for small diversions or 500 metres when you have more time.

  3. 03

    Choose categories

    Concentrate on the types of places that interest you instead of displaying every result.

  4. 04

    Explore the map

    Review suggested stops and nearby Santander Cycles docking information where available.

What it uses

A route and a curated collection.

Smart Navigation combines a mapped walking route with London Advanced’s database of unusual and overlooked places. Suggestions are selected by their relationship to the route and your chosen detour distance.

Santander Cycles information comes from Transport for London and shows nearby docking stations with current bike and space availability.

What to know

Exploration, not turn-by-turn navigation.

Street closures, temporary restrictions and walking conditions may not be reflected immediately. A nearby place is not guaranteed to be open or publicly accessible.

The selected radius is the permitted search area; actual additional walking varies with streets and entrances. Cycle availability changes quickly and should be confirmed before relying on a dock.

Worked example

Making a necessary walk worth taking.

You are walking from Waterloo to Covent Garden, have time for one interesting stop and do not want a major diversion.

  1. Enter Waterloo as the starting point and Covent Garden as the destination.
  2. Begin with a 200-metre detour and choose the categories you would genuinely stop for, such as architecture, gardens or unusual history.
  3. Inspect the suggested places against the route. If the shortlist is too thin, widen the allowance to 500 metres and compare what the extra distance adds.
  4. Check the selected place’s access details, then use a live navigation app for the final walking instructions.

The useful result: the journey remains purposeful, but one relevant stop turns it into part of the visit. A 500-metre search is not automatically better: use it only when the additional suggestion justifies the real street-level diversion. Repeat with fewer categories if the map becomes too noisy to compare.

Common questions

Distances, directions and live bikes.

What does a 200-metre or 500-metre detour mean?

It is the search distance around the mapped route, not a guarantee that the extra walk will equal that distance. Street layout, entrances and crossings determine the actual diversion.

Can Smart Navigation replace a turn-by-turn navigation app?

No. It is a discovery layer for finding worthwhile places near a walking route. Use a current navigation service for detailed directions, closures and accessibility needs.

Is Santander Cycles availability live?

Dock information comes from TfL and reflects current reported availability, but bikes and spaces can change within minutes. Recheck before depending on a particular station.
